analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | before the storm
key_insights: US S&P futures are down more than 100bps pre-market, led lower by technology shares. The desk cites META only raising the bottom end of its capex guidance, LRCX flagging supply chain, and some pointing to a TSLA capex cut. The desk calls it a tough backdrop for AI/data center names with implications for broader risk.
Overseas equities are weak: KOSPI down 350bps, Japan down 265bps, and broad Europe down 100-125bps depending on the market. Copper is down 250bps.
Crude is bid on continued escalation in tensions, including Saudi attacks. Brent is $112 and WTI is approaching $100. The desk flags fears that the midterms could be a geopolitical escalation event.

The 10-year yield is lower on growth concerns, down to 5.08%. The desk continues to believe this could drive rate-sensitive subsectors that the investment community does not own higher. The dollar is lower and Bitcoin is down 350bps to $81.7k.

Privo on Risk: confidence is shaken but AI demand still looks robust. Token consumption keeps growing, B200 compute pricing is extraordinarily firm and breaking out in the spot market, and SpaceX is talking about sub one year paybacks on new compute deployments.

Privo describes the AI worries as nearly unfalsifiable and contradictory. One worry is that the industry cannot deliver the projected gigawatts (estimates in the high 40s for 2027 versus actual delivery closer to the low 20s). The opposite worry is that too much capacity is delivered for inference demand to absorb.

Privo says hyperscalers remain the anchor for equities, telling investors demand is robust, monetization is accelerating and organic revenue and free cash flow may arrive faster than expected. The risk environment is still difficult, with credit increasingly setting the tone. Other worries are midterm and energy risk, rates, credit stress and French sovereign spreads.

Privo argues the economy has moved from a savings glut to a spending glut, with capital competing for returns. That probably demands lower multiples and greater certainty on cash flows, which is unhelpful for equities near term. Credit spreads and the availability of financing are the signals to watch.

Europe earnings reaction: SAND SS -5% on a small beat on orders, revenue and EBITDA, with Rock Processing orders missing. RTO LN +8% after ROL's North America pest control organic growth of 2.4% and a $200mm buyback. KNIN SW +2% on a beat and raise. NEX FP -5% despite a Q3 sales beat. HO FP -1% with topline 2% ahead on defense and soft digital, outlook raised. SCHN SW +7% on a Q3 beat and raise. KYGA ID +3%. METSO FH -2% with strong orders but a margin miss.
The desk says the European moves make sense if you read the releases but are not moving in favor of positioning, which it calls a difficult backdrop.

Micro items: CARR plans a $600mm Texas plant to make cooling gear for data centers. FMC is expanding its board and adding a shareholder. TT will acquire Cancoil Thermal, a heat transfer products maker.

GIR (Neil Mehta) refreshed estimates for specialty contractors PWR, MTZ and MYRG ahead of 3Q earnings, lowering price targets to reflect market uncertainty about outer-year contributions given caution around the power theme. GIR says current valuations increasingly reflect those concerns and sees an increasingly compelling risk/reward after the group's underperformance.

GIR views transmission and distribution projects from utility-scale customers as a key driver of durable earnings growth and a structural tailwind. It sees a large portion of load growth coming from non-AI factors, with data center awards an additional source of growth over the long term. It highlights a relative preference for PWR and MTZ.

AVEX fell on a Bloomberg report that the U.S. Navy suspended purchases of BlackSea Technologies' GARC vessels over performance issues. AVEX said the article has factual inaccuracies, that it delivered the original units to contract terms, and that it has been awarded additional funding for modifications and upgrades. It says its financial assumptions related to BlackSea do not change. GS (Noah) makes no model changes and is Buy rated at 12X P/E and 7X EBITDA on 2027E.
